title: Negative Numbers
description: Understanding, ordering, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing directed numbers, with real-world contexts.

notes.heading: What Are Negative Numbers?
notes.body: Negative numbers are numbers less than zero. They sit to the left of zero on a number line. We use a minus sign to show they are negative, for example -3, -10 and -25. Real-world examples include temperatures below zero, owing money (debt), floors below ground level, and elevations below sea level. Zero is neither positive nor negative.

notes.heading: Ordering Negative Numbers
notes.body: On a number line, numbers increase as you move to the right. This means any positive number is greater than any negative number. When comparing two negative numbers, the one closer to zero is greater. For example, -4 is greater than -7 because -4 is to the right of -7. Always remember: the further left a number is, the smaller it is.

notes.heading: Adding and Subtracting Negative Numbers
notes.body: Think of adding a positive number as moving right on the number line, and subtracting a positive number as moving left. Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting a positive number: 5 + (-3) = 5 - 3 = 2. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding a positive number: 4 - (-2) = 4 + 2 = 6. Two minus signs together make a plus.

notes.heading: Multiplying and Dividing Negative Numbers
notes.body: The rules for multiplying and dividing are the same. If two numbers have the same sign, the answer is positive: (-3) × (-4) = 12 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. If two numbers have different signs, the answer is negative: (-5) × 2 = -10 and 18 ÷ (-6) = -3. A common mistake is forgetting that a negative times a negative gives a positive answer.

notes.heading: Real-World Contexts
notes.body: Negative numbers appear in everyday life. Temperature: -5 degrees Celsius is 5 degrees below freezing. Elevation: -20 metres means 20 metres below sea level. Money: a balance of -£15 means you owe £15. Sports: a goal difference of -3 means you have scored 3 fewer goals than you have let in. Drawing a number line can help solve word problems.

flashcards.definition: A number that is less than zero, shown with a minus sign.
A straight line where numbers are placed in order from left to right.
A number that has a direction, either positive or negative.
flashcards.example: +5 and -5 are directed numbers with opposite directions.

flashcards.definition: The symbol < means the first number is smaller than the second.
flashcards.example: -6 < -2 because -6 is to the left of -2.

flashcards.definition: The symbol > means the first number is larger than the second.
Two minus signs next to each other become a plus.
Multiplying or dividing two numbers with the same sign gives a positive answer.
Multiplying or dividing two numbers with different signs gives a negative answer.

questions.explanation: -2 is closer to zero than -5, so -2 is greater. On a number line, -2 is to the right of -5.
Adding -6 is the same as subtracting 6. Starting at 3 and moving 6 left on the number line gives -3.
Two minus signs make a plus, so -4 - (-7) becomes -4 + 7. Count up from -4 by 7 to reach 3.
Start at -8 and move 5 places to the right. You pass -7, -6, -5, -4, -3, so the answer is -3.
Both numbers are negative, so they have the same sign. Same signs give a positive answer: 6 × 3 = 18.
The numbers have different signs, so the answer is negative. 15 ÷ 5 = 3, so 15 ÷ (-5) = -3.

questions.stem: Put these in order from smallest to largest: -1, -6, 0, 3.
questions.explanation: On a number line, the order from left to right is -6, -1, 0, 3, so that is smallest to largest.

questions.stem: The temperature was -4 degrees Celsius at 6 am. By noon it had risen by 9 degrees. What was the noon temperature?
questions.explanation: Risen means add. Start at -4 and add 9: -4 + 9 = 5. The noon temperature was 5 degrees Celsius.
Adding -5 is the same as subtracting 5. Starting at -9 and moving 5 left gives -14.

questions.stem: A diver is 12 metres below sea level. She dives another 7 metres down. How deep is she now?
questions.explanation: Below sea level can be represented by negative numbers. Start at -12 and go 7 more down: -12 + (-7) = -19, so 19 metres below sea level.
The numbers have different signs, so the answer must be negative. 2 × 8 = 16, so (-2) × 8 = -16.
Starting at 7 and moving 12 places to the left on the number line passes zero and ends at -5.
